pr.title: Enable DestinationPropagation by default.
pr.description:
~~Based on https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/115291.~~

This PR proposes to enable the destination propagation pass by default.
This pass is meant to reduce the amount of copies present in MIR.

At the same time, this PR removes the `RenameReturnPlace` pass, as it is currently unsound.
`DestinationPropagation` is not limited to `_0`, but does not handle borrowed locals.
pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.originalLogic: `RenameReturnPlace` looked for MIR that always copies the same local into the return place and eliminated that copy by renaming all uses of the source local to `_0`. Its eligibility check required that the return place not be read before `Return` and that a whole-local assignment to `_0` be the only definition reaching `Return`. The replacement pass, `DestinationPropagation`, is a more general copy/destination propagation that is "not limited to `_0`, but does not handle borrowed locals." This PR enables it by changing `sess.mir_opt_level() >= 3` to `>= 2` and moves it into the pipeline where `nrvo::RenameReturnPlace` used to run. The removed pass was explicitly guarded as unsound for issue #111005.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong transformation is `RenameReturnPlace` renaming *every* use of the copied local to `_0`, including later assignments/definitions of that local after the copy into the return place. In the supplied `nrvo_miscompile_111005` diff, the input has `_2 = _1; _0 = _2; _2 = const 'b';`, which returns the original `_1`. The old pass turns this into `_0 = _1; _0 = const 'b';`, so the post-copy write intended for `_2` now clobbers the return place and changes the result. The correction is not to blindly rename the local; `DestinationPropagation` instead produces `nop; _0 = _1; _1 = const 'b';`, preserving the value copied into `_0`. Separately, the removed pass did not restrict itself to non-borrowed locals, whereas `DestinationPropagation` deliberately "does not handle borrowed locals"; the `nrvo_borrowed` expectation shows the borrowed local `_2` remaining in place while an unrelated copy `_4 = _1` is eliminated.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR functions where a local is copied into the return place and can subsequently be assigned again, including `#[custom_mir(dialect = "runtime", phase = "initial")]` test functions that encode the exact assignment order. Also functions where the candidate local is borrowed, e.g. `_6 = &mut _2`, and ordinary functions with stack arrays passed by mutable reference. Both panic-abort and panic-unwind MIR are in scope. No compiler was built or executed; this is inferred from the supplied patch and MIR expectation diffs.
analysis.summary: Enabling `DestinationPropagation` by default replaces the removed, unsound `RenameReturnPlace` pass. The reusable correctness lesson is that renaming a local copied to the return place is invalid if that local is written again after the copy: those post-copy writes would start clobbering `_0`. A correct destination-propagation implementation must preserve the value assigned to the destination and must not treat borrowed locals as freely renameable. The retained `nrvo_miscompile_111005` test name/comment alone does not prove the replacement pass is wrong; the decoded assignments show the old pass corrupting the return value, while the replacement preserves it.
analysis.trigger: A local is copied into the return place, and then that same source local is assigned a new value before the `Return`; or the local is borrowed. `RenameReturnPlace`'s eligibility check only considered the copy reaching `Return`, so it missed the later write and renamed it to `_0`.
preconditions: Candidate MIR has a whole-local assignment into the return place, e.g. `_0 = _2`, reaching `Return`.
The source local has a later assignment after that copy, e.g. `_2 = const 'b';`, which the old pass also renames.
The return place may not have been read before `Return`; that condition alone is insufficient to make renaming sound.
Borrowed locals must be excluded from destination propagation; `DestinationPropagation` does not handle them.
The replacement pass is enabled at `mir_opt_level >= 2`, not only at level 3.
pitfalls: Do not conflate the post-copy overwrite bug with the borrowed-local restriction; they are separate reasons a naive rename is unsafe.
A retained test filename or comment mentioning `nrvo_miscompile_111005` does not establish that `DestinationPropagation` is incorrect; compare the actual value assignments in the decoded old/new MIR.
Renaming only uses but not later definitions is unsound: post-copy writes to the source local become writes to `_0`.
`RenameReturnPlace` was removed because it was unsound, so expecting it to run is wrong; `DestinationPropagation` is the replacement in the pipeline.
Do not claim runtime reproduction or compiler execution; the patch only contains MIR expectations and source changes.
For borrowed locals, `DestinationPropagation` may leave the copy in place; absence of NRVO-like elimination there is conservative behavior, not a miscompile.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `//@ test-mir-pass: DestinationPropagation` with `// EMIT_MIR ...DestinationPropagation.diff` and, where relevant, `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`. Build focused `custom_mir` cases whose input MIR differs only in whether the source local is overwritten after `_0 = local`; assert the after-pass MIR does not assign `_0` from that later write and that the copied value remains in `_0`. Add a borrowed-local case (`&mut local` before the copy) and assert the pass conservatively leaves the borrowed local/copy rather than renaming it into `_0`. Keep the old `RenameReturnPlace` miscompile test as a regression for the replacement pass, but inspect actual assignments rather than trusting the retained "miscompilation" comment. No execution or reproduction is claimed here.
